instructions:
Extract the clinical assertions and supported relationships from the supplied letters, then answer each question about its index date using only these letters. Return an object containing annotations (matching annotation_schema) and answers (matching answer_schema).
Preserve the interpretation expressed in each letter, even when a later letter revises it. Keep reporter disagreement unresolved unless the text explicitly settles the disputed fact. Later evidence can explain an earlier event but a subsequent new event does not change an earlier absence interval. Repeated text is not independent corroboration. Leave uncertain event identity unresolved.
Keep clinical dates separate from letter availability. Preserve endpoint uncertainty and original time wording; do not invent exact dates for vague seasons. Current assertions do not establish unobserved earlier or later intervals. A continuing documented diagnosis can persist until revised. Preserve rates, counts, cluster counts and events per cluster separately. Do not infer a diagnosis from medication or test results.
Use eligible when all necessary conditions are supported, ineligible when evidence refutes a necessary condition, and indeterminate when information is missing or an unresolved conflict can change the answer. To answer ineligible because no qualifying event or action exists, require complete evidence for the relevant scope and timeframe. No clinical content means no clinical assertions, not negative clinical findings.
Evidence quotes must exactly match the unchanged source. Offsets count Unicode characters from zero; end is exclusive. Give each answer its request_id, status, supporting evidence and a plain explanation. Cite supporting evidence from multiple letters where the decision requires it.

documents.text:
Epilepsy clinic letter
Consultation: 05 March 2025
Patient: Laura Chen, aged 28

Dear colleague,

Laura attended our clinic following referral for episodic paroxysmal sensory symptoms.

She describes episodes of sudden visual scintillations followed by dizziness and paresthesia in the left hand lasting 10 to 15 minutes, occurring roughly weekly, with the latest episode on 28 February 2025. Her clinical assessment is challenging. The differential diagnosis includes focal sensory epilepsy, migraine aura without headache, or vestibular events. I cannot establish a definitive diagnosis of epilepsy today, and the clinical picture remains indeterminate. She takes no anti-seizure medications.

We arranged brain MRI and routine outpatient EEG. Follow-up in four months.

Laura says she has never lost awareness during her sensory episodes. Her mother reports that Laura did not respond to her voice during the episode on 28 February and believes awareness was lost. Laura disputes this account. I have not resolved this reporter disagreement; neither report settles the epilepsy versus migraine differential.

Epilepsy clinic letter
Consultation: 16 July 2025
Patient: Laura Chen

Dear colleague,

I reviewed Laura today. Her brain MRI was completely normal.

She continues to experience weekly sensory episodes, with the latest on 10 July 2025. Routine EEG showed non-specific theta slowing without epileptiform discharges. Having reviewed detailed symptom logs, focal aware sensory seizures remain a leading possibility, but migraine aura without headache remains an equally plausible differential. The diagnostic categorization remains uncertain and unresolved.

No anti-seizure medication commenced. We agreed to arrange prolonged ambulatory EEG monitoring. Follow-up in four months.

query_definitions.Q1: Documented epilepsy at the index date and at least one event interpreted as epileptic in the supplied 90-day timeframe. Explicit absence of all epileptic seizures throughout that timeframe can refute. Missing evidence is indeterminate.
query_definitions.Q2: At least two distinct patterns interpreted as epileptic, with overlapping active intervals within the supplied 90-day timeframe. An explicit complete inventory of at most one active epileptic pattern throughout the timeframe can refute. Different names need not mean different patterns.
query_definitions.Q3: The named medication was actually started within the supplied 180-day timeframe. A plan or prescription is not confirmed use. Explicit non-initiation throughout the timeframe can refute. Current use alone does not date initiation.
query_definitions.Q4: A test of the named modality requested within the supplied 180-day timeframe has a result clinically available by the index date. Match the particular request to its result. The result availability date differs from the letter availability date. One pending or unrelated older test cannot exclude other qualifying requests when the request inventory is incomplete.
query_definitions.Q5: A previously documented epileptic event or pattern with an occurrence in the supplied 180-day timeframe was explicitly reinterpreted as non-epileptic by the index date. Require identity, an earlier interpretation and a dated revision. A later decision cannot be moved back to the index date. Absence of a revision alone is indeterminate.

assertions.description: Statements preserved separately from each supplied letter.

links.description: Supported relationships; leave uncertain identity unresolved.

DateBounds.description: Bounds on one endpoint, not an interval between two events.

Time.description: Time supported by the text. An uncertain endpoint has bounds; an unstated endpoint is null.

anyOf.description: Source time expression; null when not stated.

kind.description: What the time describes. Result availability refers to the clinical team.

anyOf.description: Letter whose visit date anchors a relative or implicit current time; null if no anchor is needed.

Span.description: Exact evidence in an unchanged letter.

start.description: Zero-based character position of the first quoted character.

end.description: Character position immediately after the quote.

text.description: Exact quote, including punctuation and spaces.

Quantity.description: Inclusive numerical bounds. Null bounds preserve unspecified amounts; do not invent a midpoint.

anyOf.description: Lowest supported amount; null when unspecified.
Highest supported amount; null when unspecified.

lower_inclusive.description: False for a strict lower bound; omitted means inclusive.

upper_inclusive.description: False for a strict upper bound; omitted means inclusive.

Period.description: Time basis of a reported rate.

unit.description: Time unit as documented; do not convert months to days.

Burden.description: Preserve counts, time basis, ranges and cluster structure separately. For freedom, period is the stated duration.

kind.description: Rate, interval count, clusters, seizure-free duration, or words without a recoverable number.

approximate.description: True when the source qualifies the amount as approximate.

Diagnosis.description: An epilepsy diagnosis assertion; a seizure description is not a diagnosis.

name.description: Documented epilepsy diagnosis, preserving unspecified type.

phase.description: Whether the diagnosis applies now or is described as past.

Seizure.description: Seizure-related information, including explicitly non-epileptic events.

names.description: One name per pattern; several only for an explicit inventory.

kind.description: A dated event, recurring pattern, explicit absence, or stated complete/incomplete list.

interpretation.description: Interpretation asserted in this letter, not the latest interpretation elsewhere.

scope.description: Whether the assertion concerns a named pattern, all epileptic events, or all reported event types.

Medication.description: A medication statement; silence does not establish non-use.

status.description: Keep a plan or prescription separate from reported use.

anyOf.description: Condition stated for a conditional action.

Investigation.description: An investigation assertion; identical modalities need not identify the same test.

modality.description: Named test modality such as EEG or MRI.

status.description: Keep request, performance and result separate; inventory describes all requests in an interval.

anyOf.description: Reported result, without inferring a diagnosis.
Count only for an explicitly enumerated request inventory.

Assertion.description: One attributable assertion about one clinical fact and time. Split changing statuses into separate assertions.

assertion_id.description: Unique ID for this statement. Preserve an earlier ID when later text disagrees.

letter_id.description: ID of the letter making the statement.

evidence.description: Quotes supporting this statement, its scope and qualifications.

reporter.description: Whose assertion is recorded; mixed only when agreement is explicitly reported.

certainty.description: Certainty expressed in the text, not confidence in the extraction.

polarity.description: Whether the statement is asserted or denied. Do not negate a not_started status twice.

coverage.description: Complete only when the text explicitly exhausts the named scope and interval.

Link.description: A supported relationship. Keep both endpoint assertions; do not overwrite either one.

relation.description: How the assertions relate. A correction requires explicit reinterpretation of the same event.

certainty.description: Whether identity and relationship are supported or remain unresolved.

evidence.description: Text supporting identity and the relationship, not merely the existence of both assertions.
Exact supporting quotes from supplied letters.

reason.description: Explain what supports, refutes or leaves the requested condition unresolved.

Span.description: Exact evidence in an unchanged letter.

start.description: Zero-based character position of the first quoted character.

end.description: Character position immediately after the quote.

text.description: Exact quote, including punctuation and spaces.
